title: Joe Loco leaves for Arnold Shaw's agency
summary: After McRae built him up with three dates a night, Loco jumped to a new agent, and radio disc jockeys dropped his records.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: So one day, Joe came --
Arnold Shaw?
Arnold Shaw.
One day, Joe come to me and says, he wanted two thousand dollars. You know, we was working like we was working --
We wouldn't take any (inaudible). We'd take like four hundred and fifty dollars and do two hours, (Inaudible) so and so at 168th Street.
We worked like three dates in one night.
St. George Hotel, part of that circuit too, down in Brooklyn?
MR. MC RAE: Yeah, anywhere. We take, like, Brooklyn -- anywhere. We take like three dates.
We'd open up, you know -- Joe Loco. Like they have three latin bands. Not all the (inaudible) for Joe could go -- play two hours here, give him a

And we was getting like four hundred and fifty, five hundred dollars for each date.
Then playing Monday night in Newark, he get about six hundred dollars.
Had a nice crowd?
And then he --
I told his wife -- I says, 'Can your husband handle this money?'
She say, 'Oh, yeah, I'll help him handle his money.'
'Because I'm gonna make him a lot of money.' Then I get a call from Joe (inaudible). He say he wanted three thousand dollars.
I say, 'What big agent hitting on you now wanna give you a contract?' So he told me Arnold Shaw.
So I called and I say -- Shaw and I were good friends. I say, 'Hey, you want my artist, huh?' Because I didn't have no contract on him. I say, 'Well

See, what happened, the disc jockeys found out -- remember I'm working with all the colored disc jockeys on this Latin (this) (inaudible). The guys in Newark, Jack Walker, the guys in Philly. I took him to Philly, the three T's of Philly. Tito Puente, Tito Rodriguez and somebody else with a T. I took three bands down there. They had a packed house. Packed. And they found out that Joe Loco had jumped and left me and went to Shaw Agency. That was the end of it. They pulled the records, you know. You can't do that. And he got (inaudible) some fella out of Philadelphia to book him and nothing happened with them. Because -- see, he went with somebody that (didn't) (inaudible) understand what was going on that time. You see, it was a certain area that Latin was popular in -- they were coming up. You had to --

Yeah, around that time. Because I had went to Philly and asked the kids at one of the big dancers down there -- I say, "what do yall think about the Latin," you know. They say, "Yeah, man, bring somebody in." So I took Joe and them -- took Tito Puente, Tito Rodriguez down there, had a big thing up in North Philly -- big ballroom. It was packed.
Blue Horizon?

Yeah, big, big, thing. And we was supposed to go to Cleveland and Detroit. He didn't -- they -- I say, "Well I'm making a agent." I'm paying their agent too. You know, I got to pay this agent because I'm booking the band and we're splitting he commission, you know.
Yeah.
I didn't split commission on
